analysis.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject, אֶת marks הָאוֹר as the object, and כִּי טוֹב states what God perceived about the light: it was good.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־ and an apocopated verb form.
analysis.sense: see or perceive that something is so

analysis.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject of וַיַּרְא (“he saw”), a masculine singular verb. The singular agreement identifies God as the one who saw that the light was good.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine plural absolute, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים אֶת הָאוֹר, God is the subject of וַיַּרְא ‘saw’, and אֶת marks הָאוֹר ‘the light’ as the definite direct object.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected direct-object particle without prefix or suffix

analysis.evidence: אֶת marks הָאוֹר as the object of וַיַּרְא, “he saw.” God sees that the light is good, then separates that same light from הַחֹשֶׁךְ, “the darkness.”
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ + common noun אוֹר, common gender, singular absolute.

analysis.evidence: וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים אֶת הָאוֹר identifies the light as what God saw. כִּי introduces the judgment טוֹב about the light: God saw that it was good.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected conjunction without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: that (what is seen, known or said)

analysis.evidence: God sees the light (הָאוֹר), and כִּי טוֹב gives his assessment, “that it was good.” טוֹב agrees with הָאוֹר in gender and number.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute adjective, used predicatively.

draft.change: Add the Hebrew verb בָּדַל with its Hiphil sense of separating.
draft.definition: To separate one thing from another.
draft.evidence: In Gen.1.4, God separates light from darkness. The repeated בֵּין introduces each member of the pair.

analysis.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject of וַיַּבְדֵּל. The paired phrases בֵּין הָאוֹר וּבֵין הַחֹשֶׁךְ identify the two things God separated, light and darkness.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil wayyiqtol, third masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־ and no suffix.
analysis.sense: to separate one thing from another

analysis.evidence: The marked אֱלֹהִים is the subject of וַיַּבְדֵּל, “he separated.” The verb is third-person masculine singular, identifying God as the one who separated the light from the darkness.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine plural, absolute state, with singular agreement. No prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: After וַיַּבְדֵּל ‘he separated,’ the marked בֵּין introduces הָאוֹר ‘the light.’ The paired וּבֵין introduces הַחֹשֶׁךְ ‘the darkness,’ identifying the two things God separated.
analysis.morphology: Preposition in the construct form בֵּין, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In בֵּין הָאוֹר וּבֵין הַחֹשֶׁךְ, the marked הָאוֹר names the light that God separates from the darkness.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ + common noun, common gender, singular absolute.

analysis.evidence: In בֵּין הָאוֹר וּבֵין הַחֹשֶׁךְ ‘between the light and the darkness’, וּבֵין introduces the second member of the pair that God separates with וַיַּבְדֵּל.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וּ־ ‘and’ prefixed to the preposition בֵין, with no suffix.

analysis.evidence: In בֵּין הָאוֹר וּבֵין הַחֹשֶׁךְ, God separates the light from the darkness. The pairing with הָאוֹר gives הַחֹשֶׁךְ its literal sense.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, with prefixed definite article הַ־.
